title: Balance seesaw and center of mass

data.title: Balance seesaw and center of mass
data.statement:
Read an ASCII drawing of a seesaw. Output the support column, the horizontal center of mass, and whether the seesaw is in balance.

The drawing has [[h]] rows and [[w]] columns. Blocks are stacked on a continuous surface. Each {{#}} represents an equal mass at the center of its column. Spaces have no mass. The last drawing row contains the support, marked by {{X}}. The support has no mass. The {{#}} characters in the surface do contribute mass.

Columns are numbered from {{0}} on the left. The horizontal <<center of mass>> is the average column number of all {{#}} characters. Vertical positions do not affect this value.

The support is centered on the column of {{X}} and is one column wide: it extends half a column to each side. The seesaw is in balance when its center of mass is inside this interval, <<including both edges>>. Determine balance using the exact center of mass, before rounding it for output.

Print the support column and the center of mass, followed by {{In balance}} or {{Not in balance}} on the next line.
data.constraints:
2 ≤ [[h]] ≤ 100
1 ≤ [[w]] ≤ 500
The complete input contains at most {{10000}} characters.
The first [[h]] − 1 drawing rows contain only {{#}} and spaces, with at least one {{#}} in total.
Drawing row [[h]] − 1 is a continuous surface of {{#}} characters, optionally surrounded by spaces.
Drawing row [[h]] contains exactly one {{X}} and otherwise only spaces.
Every {{#}} above the surface has another {{#}} directly below it.
The {{X}} is directly below a {{#}} of the surface.

lastVersion.statementHTML:
Goal

Read an ASCII drawing of a seesaw. Output the support column, the horizontal center of mass, and whether the seesaw is in balance.

The drawing has h rows and w columns. Blocks are stacked on a continuous surface. Each # represents an equal mass at the center of its column. Spaces have no mass. The last drawing row contains the support, marked by X. The support has no mass. The # characters in the surface do contribute mass.

Columns are numbered from 0 on the left. The horizontal center of mass is the average column number of all # characters. Vertical positions do not affect this value.

The support is centered on the column of X and is one column wide: it extends half a column to each side. The seesaw is in balance when its center of mass is inside this interval, including both edges. Determine balance using the exact center of mass, before rounding it for output.

Print the support column and the center of mass, followed by In balance or Not in balance on the next line.
Input
Line 1: Two space-separated integers h and w, the height and width of the drawing.
Next h lines: A string line of exactly w characters containing one drawing row.
Output
Line 1: The support column as an integer and the center of mass rounded to exactly six digits after the decimal point, separated by one space. Use . as the decimal separator and include trailing zeros.
Line 2: In balance if the exact center of mass is within the support interval, including its edges. Otherwise, Not in balance.
Constraints
2 ≤ h ≤ 100
1 ≤ w ≤ 500
The complete input contains at most 10000 characters.
The first h − 1 drawing rows contain only # and spaces, with at least one # in total.
Drawing row h − 1 is a continuous surface of # characters, optionally surrounded by spaces.
Drawing row h contains exactly one X and otherwise only spaces.
Every # above the surface has another # directly below it.
The X is directly below a # of the surface.
Example
Input
4 21
#                    
#####            ####
#####################
         X
Output
9 9.483871
In balance
